item.title: A40 Westway shut for five weeks in major TfL safety works
item.description: Image credit: TfL Transport for London (TfL) will close the A40 Westway between the A40 Westway Roundabout and the Marylebone Flyover from 20 March until late April to carry out what it describes as essential safety-critical renewal works. The closure will affect one of the capital’s busiest strategic roads, which TfL says is used by up to 96,000 vehicles a day. item.title: LICENCE SURRENDERED: Uber quits Southend market weeks after green light
item.description: Uber has surrendered its private hire operator licence to operate in Southend-on-Sea, less than two months after being formally approved by the city council to enter the local market. Southend-on-Sea City Council said it had been informed by Uber Britannia Limited that the company had chosen to give up its licence, bringing an early end to its plans to operate in the city. item.title: Arrests made after brutal taxi driver attack sees cabbie hospitalised and cash stolen
item.description: Two people remain in police custody after a taxi driver was assaulted and robbed in the early hours of this morning in Newcastle. Police said officers were called shortly after midnight following multiple 999 reports of a disturbance on Roman Avenue in the Walker area of the city. When officers arrived, they found a taxi driver injured in the road after being threatened and assaulted by passengers. item.title: Huntingdonshire Council suspends or revokes 25 taxi and PHV licences over six month period
item.description: Huntingdonshire District Council suspended or revoked 25 hackney carriage and private hire licences in the six months to January 2026, with dangerous and major vehicle defects driving most enforcement action, according to a report presented to councillors. Figures submitted to the council’s Licensing and Protection Committee show that 23 vehicle licences and two dual driver licences were suspended or revoked between 1 September 2025 and 10 January 2026. item.title: Central Bedfordshire Council shake-up mandates council-run depots for six-monthly taxi MOTs
item.description: Central Bedfordshire Council has approved changes to its taxi and private hire vehicle testing regime that will require all eligible licensed vehicles to undergo their six-monthly MOT inspections at council-designated depots. The update to the authority’s Private Hire and Hackney Carriage Policy was agreed by Full Council on Thursday 29 January and aligns the six-monthly MOT requirement with the annual compliance testing already carried out by the council. item.title: NPHTA warns MPs national taxi standards will fail without fee reform, statutory intended use and tougher enforcement
item.description: The National Private Hire and Taxi Association (NPHTA) has submitted detailed supplementary evidence to the Transport Select Committee, arguing that proposed national standards for the taxi and private hire sector will not deliver meaningful reform unless they address licensing fees, enforcement practices and intended use rules through primary legislation. item.title: Charnwood Council to tighten taxi emissions and testing rules from April 2026
item.description: Charnwood Borough Council is set to introduce stricter emissions standards and revised vehicle testing rules for hackney carriage and private hire vehicles from April 2026, following approval of a comprehensive licensing policy review by councillors. item.title: LOWER ENTRY BARRIER: Council scraps taxi knowledge test in bid to boost driver numbers
item.description: South Kesteven District Council has formally approved a refreshed Hackney Carriage and Private Hire Licensing Policy, adopting a package of changes aimed at reducing barriers to entry for new drivers while maintaining statutory safety standards. item.title: MAKING TAX DIGITAL: Taxi association warns drivers taking over £50,000 face digital tax reporting from April 2026
item.description: Taxi drivers with self-employment revenue above £50,000 will be required to comply with Making Tax Digital for Income Tax from 6 April 2026, marking a significant shift in how earnings and expenses are recorded and reported to the tax authority. Under the changes, affected drivers will no longer submit just a single annual Self Assessment return.
